dish: pollo a la brasa (charcoal rotisserie chicken) with green sauce
w: Arlington's legendary Peruvian charcoal-chicken counter in Virginia Square, a decades-old cult institution whose aroma reaches a block away; a Washingtonian award winner for Best Peruvian Chicken and a Roadfood-anointed classic.

dish: Texas-style beef brisket, beef short ribs, house sausage
w: Lone Star-style smoked brisket and beef ribs in Lyon Park; named the No. 1 best barbecue joint in the DC area by the Washington Post multiple years running and a fixture of the Arlington dining scene since 2015.

dish: smoked brisket, sticky spare ribs, biscuit sandwiches, meat-and-three
w: James Beard-nominated chef Matt Hill's family-friendly Southern smokehouse; a 2022 RAMMY winner and voted the No. 1 reader-favorite restaurant in Virginia by Washingtonian, with a Washington Post rave for its barbecue and brunch biscuits.

dish: wood-smoked meats, house-made pasta, Sunday supper
w: Clarendon's benchmark neighborhood restaurant, on Washingtonian's 100 Very Best list for eight consecutive years with multiple RAMMY nominations and a Washington Post Editor's Pick; everything from bread to pasta is made in-house.

dish: French onion soup, steak frites, French New-American bistro plates
w: A chic French New-American bistro in the heart of Clarendon executing comforting classics with classic French technique; reviewed favorably by Northern Virginia Magazine and covered as a Clarendon draw by ARLnow.

dish: lamb plov, manti dumplings, samsa
w: The area's only Russian-Uzbek kitchen, a family-run Ballston spot whose plov and manti dumplings drew a Washingtonian recommendation and a Northern Virginia Magazine Best Restaurants nod.

dish: grilled octopus, whole fish, lamb, Greek meze
w: The upscale modern-Greek destination of Tysons/Vienna, a repeat Washingtonian 100 Very Best and ranked No. 2 on Northern Virginia Magazine's 2025 list of the 50 Best Restaurants in Northern Virginia.

dish: kabuli pulao, aushak dumplings, lamb-and-okra stew
w: Upscale Afghan cooking in McLean from the acclaimed Aracosia family; a Washingtonian 100 Very Best (2025 and 2026) whose sibling rooms Tom Sietsema of the Washington Post called the area's best Afghan.

dish: seasonal prix-fixe with a Lithuanian twist
w: A tiny women- and Latina-owned modern-European bistro in Vienna by chef Juste; a Washingtonian 100 Very Best pick and No. 9 on Northern Virginia Magazine's 50 Best list, known for its seasonal prix-fixe.

dish: kubideh kebab, salmon kabob, shirin polo
w: A 27-year family-run Persian kebab house in a McLean strip mall whose kubideh and shirin polo earned a Washingtonian Cheap Eats nod and a Northern Virginia Magazine 'latest obsession' feature; Google 4.4 across 250+ reviews.

dish: binchotan robata skewers, sushi, izakaya small plates
address: 1825 Capital One Dr S, Tysons, VA 22102
w: A Japanese izakaya with binchotan robata and panoramic views atop the Watermark Hotel; on Washingtonian's Best Restaurants shortlist and named to the Washington Post's 25 best new restaurants of its year.

dish: Turkish kebabs, mezze, the orange baklava
w: A McLean Turkish institution since 1980, reviewed repeatedly by the Washington Post; owner Zeynel Uzun's orange baklava is the same sweet Queen Elizabeth II proclaimed her favorite on a 1971 visit to Turkey.

dish: from-scratch farm-to-table plates, house-baked bread, craft cocktails
w: The farmer-owned, wildly popular flagship on the Silver Line at Reston Station; a multi-year RAMMY honoree from Farmers Restaurant Group and named the best farm-to-table in DC by Travel + Leisure, everything made from scratch.

dish: ceviche, lomo saltado, pisco cocktails
w: A bright Peruvian ceviche gastrobar at Reston Town Center bringing inventive Latin American plates and pisco to the Dulles corridor; a Northern Virginia Magazine First Bite review pick and a Visit Fairfax listing.

dish: veal chop, house pastas, red-sauce Tuscan classics
w: An old-world, candlelit Tuscan-Italian room in a century-old Herndon building, a white-tablecloth destination since 1991 famed for its veal chop; carries a 4.6 rating across 4,000-plus reviews and a longtime GAYOT recommendation.

dish: pho-spiced French onion soup, kimchi-tofu bouillabaisse, comfort food
w: The Falls Church comfort-food restaurant from Yuan and Carey Tang of Michelin-starred Rooster & Owl; winner of the 2024 RAMMY for New Restaurant of the Year and a Washingtonian 100 Very Best, with a New York Times nod.

dish: handmade pasta (pappardelle with wild-boar ragu), olive-oil cake
address: 124 N Washington St, Falls Church, VA 22046
w: A husband-and-wife pasta-and-pastry powerhouse (Gabe from Le Bernardin, Katherine from Per Se) that has landed on Washingtonian's 100 Very Best repeatedly; a beloved Falls Church neighborhood Italian.

dish: creative tacos, tortas, al pastor
w: Chef Victor Albisu's original Falls Church taqueria (2013), the cult-following flagship of the Taco Bamba empire; the James Beard semifinalist's creative tacos were called some of the best on the East Coast by Esquire.

dish: all-you-can-eat Korean barbecue, banchan
w: The standout of Annandale's Koreatown for tableside grilling, a Washingtonian 100 Very Best and Cheap Eats favorite whose meat quality and banchan spread set it above the block's many barbecue rooms.

dish: Peking duck carved tableside
w: The famous Falls Church Peking-duck house since 1978 and a Bush-family favorite (their booth got Secret Service bulletproof glass); its lacquered duck is a Washingtonian-lauded regional institution.

dish: beef noodle soup, braised pork rice, Taiwanese small plates
w: A cash-friendly Annandale outpost of the Taiwanese Tang-family chain, serving authentic Taiwanese and Northern Chinese street snacks; a longtime Washingtonian Cheap Eats pick and a Tyler Cowen ethnic-dining favorite.

dish: banh mi (grilled-pork and meatball), pho
w: A go-to banh mi and Vietnamese deli inside Eden Center, the largest Vietnamese commercial hub on the East Coast; a repeat pick on Arlington Magazine's best-Vietnamese roundups and the Washington Post's Eden Center guide.

dish: soondubu (soft-tofu stew), kimchi jjigae, galbitang
w: A homey Annandale specialist in comforting Korean soups and stews, singled out by Washingtonian among the best cheap Korean around DC and featured on Visit Fairfax's Koreatown tours.

dish: Chengdu-style Sichuan, dry-fried and mala dishes
w: Despite the Cantonese name, a Seven Corners Sichuan kitchen widely rated among the best in the area; a two-time Washingtonian Cheap Eats pick and a Tyler Cowen and Northern Virginia Magazine favorite for authentic Chengdu cooking.

dish: fresh house-made tofu (lemongrass, mushroom), che
w: Eden Center's famous fresh-tofu shop, making silky tofu in a range of flavors plus Vietnamese desserts; a signature stop on Arlington Magazine's Eden Center guide and Vietcetera's essential Little Saigon list.

dish: banana-blossom salad, khao soi duck curry, crispy pork belly
w: Chef Songtham Pinyolaksana's Merrifield Thai kitchen turning out consistently original, refined regional dishes; ranked No. 19 on Washingtonian's 100 Very Best and a longtime Tyler Cowen ethnic-dining pick.

dish: prime and aged-beef Korean barbecue 'guides' (set menus)
w: A Centreville Korean barbecue specialist offering prime and aged beef arranged in curated set-menu 'guides'; named to Washingtonian's 100 Very Best (2025) and Northern Virginia Magazine's 50 Best.

dish: seafood and steaks in a New England boathouse setting
w: A Fairfax City favorite from the beloved Great American Restaurants group since 1978, called 'the very best in Fairfax' by Washingtonian; a perennially packed, no-reservations American seafood-and-steak house.

dish: Thai curries and noodles in a whimsical living-room setting
w: The viral, whimsically-decorated Thai cafe at the Mosaic District, the owner's top-selling location; a Northern Virginia Magazine and Arlington Magazine favorite whose Instagram-famous rooms and Thai comfort food draw crowds.

dish: curated wine list, charcuterie, small plates
w: Old Town Fairfax's standout wine bar, voted Best Wine Bar by Northern Virginia Magazine three years running and Best Wine List by Virginia Living; a convivial small-plates-and-bottles room.
